sections.heading: Modified Bitumen vs. TPO: Advantages and Disadvantages

runs.v: used for decades on residential and commercial flat roofs, modified bitumen is widely used on low-slope roofs because its multiple reinforced plies give built-in redundancy against leaks, superior waterproofing, and superior puncture and tear resistance against foot traffic and debris, more than EPDM. SBS rubber modifiers keep it flexible in freezing temperatures, suiting properties with big temperature swings, and it is cost-efficient, low-upkeep, and easy to repair, giving long-term durability, reliable long-term protection, and long-term value on low-slope systems.

it is heavier and more labor-intensive than single-ply, torch work must follow local fire safety codes, trapped moisture can blister the plies, seams must be properly detailed, and standard dark cap sheets absorb heat unless a reflective coating or white-granule cap sheet reflects sunlight to cut cooling loads and make the roof energy efficient; a granulated cap can also add curb appeal where a low roof shows.

TPO is a lighter single ply with heat-welded seams, often rated the most energy-efficient flat roofing system, while modified bitumen handles heavy foot traffic around rooftop equipment; modified bitumen is often cited at 20 to 30 years with proper maintenance and EPDM at a similar 20 to 30, so contractors who give a straight answer will price both roofing solutions.

faqs.q: Is modified bitumen a good choice for a Bloomfield two-family or commercial roof?

runs.v: Yes, where rooftop equipment brings foot traffic and tool drops: the multi-ply assembly absorbs them, and a granulated cap sheet gives Bloomfield homeowners and commercial buildings a walkable surface.

faqs.q: What is the difference between SBS and APP modified bitumen?

runs.v: The choice sets flexibility versus heat resistance: SBS contains styrene-butadiene-styrene rubber modifiers that stay flexible through temperature changes, while APP is infused with atactic polypropylene, a plastic polymer, for heat resistance and UV stability but is stiffer in cold, so Newark Quality Roofing installs SBS for the Bloomfield freeze-thaw climate, per ARMA modified-bitumen guidance.

faqs.q: Can modified bitumen be installed without a torch on my occupied Bloomfield building?

runs.v: Yes. Modified bitumen goes down torch-applied, self-adhered, or cold-applied: torch-applied systems use a propane torch and a fire watch, per NRCA hot-work guidance, while self-adhered sheets activate a factory adhesive when the release liner peels off and cold-applied SBS uses adhesive instead of heat and stays flexible in cold weather.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a modified bitumen roof in Bloomfield, NJ?

runs.v: Re-roofing the covering on a detached one- or two-family home counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, with no construction permit. On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit, so confirm the scope with the Township of Bloomfield construction office.

faqs.q: Does a historic-listed Bloomfield property restrict a modified bitumen roof?

runs.v: It can: a property in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the Township of Bloomfield construction office before work. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private property owner.
